title: The sheaf dual-tensor-Hom morphism is the closed categorical comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and M,N any O_X-modules. Write M^\vee=\mathcal Hom(M,O_X). The morphism M^\vee\otimes N\to\mathcal Hom(M,N) defined by sheafifying the presheaf map phi tensor n mapped to (m mapped to phi(m)n) equals the canonical closed-category map obtained by transposing the evaluation-and-multiplication morphism M\otimes(M^\vee\otimes N)\to N.

source.place: Canonical tensor-Hom morphism, generalized to target N; the bridge compares its two library constructions.

proof.text: Transpose both maps under the tensor-Hom adjunction. For ihomUnitTensorToIhom, uncurry_curry makes the transpose the associator followed by internal evaluation and left unitor. For dualTensorHom, use the definition of SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv: this adjunction is built from the sheafification adjunction and PresheafOfModules.homObjEquiv.

Both underlying maps on pure tensors m tensor (phi tensor n) are phi(m)n. Tensor induction gives equality. Naturality of the tensor and unit isomorphisms for sheafification transports that equality to the sheaf maps. Injectivity of transposition gives equality of the comparisons.

proof_origin.place: Canonical tensor-Hom morphism, generalized to target N; the bridge compares its two library constructions.
proof_origin.note: The source names the canonical map; the equality between the library implementations is expanded by transposition and the construction of the sheafification adjunction.
